Evaluation metrics for Machine Translation (MT) mainly rely on comparisons with human-crafted reference sentences. Most frequently used metrics count the number of matching tokens between the reference and candidate sentences or estimate the similarity within the embedding space.

The datasets employ two distinct forms of annotations for human ratings, namely Direct Assessments (DA) and Multidimensional Quality Metrics (MQM). DA ratings are derived from crowd‑sourced evaluations, with scores ranging from 0 to 100. MQM ratings are determined by experts, using a comprehensive set of error annotations and guidelines.
